subject: Retroactive usage offset & VAT split for April surge
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@pairtree.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Pairtree Labs Billing <billing@pairtree.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: April invoice and spike — request for retro offset & VAT handling

Hi Jonas,

Hope you're well. We received invoice #PP-2025-04 (attached) and noticed our April usage was ~3.4x our baseline due to a one-week load test. We understand usage-based billing is expected, but this was a constrained, non-production test we coordinated with your solutions engineer.

Can Redwood apply a retroactive offset/credit for the test window (April 5–11) as a one-time courtesy? Also, please confirm how the credit will be reflected for EU VAT purposes — Pairtree is VAT-registered; we need an invoice with the credit line and VAT calculations for our accounts payable.

Attaching the invoice and test schedule for reference. We can escalate to procurement if you need an official PO.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Finance, Pairtree Labs
[Attachment: Pairtree_invoice_2025-04.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@pairtree.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Pairtree Labs Billing <billing@pairtree.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: April invoice and spike — request for retro offset & VAT handling

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear write-up and the invoice. I remember the test; our solutions team flagged it as a planned non-prod burst.

Proposed next steps (so Finance has what it needs):
- Redwood will issue a one-time goodwill/service credit that offsets the test-week usage.
- Credit will be issued as a negative line item on a revised invoice; VAT will be handled as an adjustment (we will reissue the invoice for net amount and include VAT reconciliation lines so your AP can ingest it).
- I’ve looped in Marissa (Finance) to confirm the credit amount and the VAT breakdown. Marcus from Billing Ops is CC'd to schedule the invoice reissue and attach the credit note PDF.

Can you confirm the exact date range for the test window you want covered and whether Pairtree needs the credit to be net of VAT or gross (i.e., show VAT on the credit line vs. crediting after VAT)? We can do either; we just need it specified for our accounting treatment.

Thanks — I’ll push this through once Finance confirms.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (415) 555-0136
jonas@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@pairtree.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Pairtree Labs Billing <billing@pairtree.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: April invoice and spike — request for retro offset & VAT handling

On Fri, Apr 18, 2025 at 10:04 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed next steps (so Finance has what it needs):
> - Redwood will issue a one-time goodwill/service credit that offsets the test-week usage.
> - Credit will be issued as a negative line item on a revised invoice; VAT will be handled as an adjustment (we will reissue the invoice for net amount and include VAT reconciliation lines so your AP can ingest it).
> - I’ve looped in Marissa (Finance) to confirm the credit amount and the VAT breakdown. Marcus from Billing Ops is CC'd to schedule the invoice reissue and attach the credit note PDF.

Thanks for pulling this together, Jonas — and hi Priya.

I reviewed the usage and confirmed the spike dates you listed (Apr 5 00:00 UTC — Apr 11 23:59 UTC). We propose the following accounting treatment:

1) Credit amount: We will credit 100% of the incremental overage above your Normalized Monthly Baseline for that week. In plain terms, we calculate your typical daily usage for March, multiply by seven, and subtract from the surge consumption — the resulting delta is credited back.

2) VAT handling: Because Pairtree is EU VAT-registered, Redwood will issue a revised invoice where the credit is applied against the taxable base; VAT will be recalculated on the net amount and shown explicitly on the credit note. That revised invoice and a separate PDF credit note will be uploaded to your HubSpot deal and sent to billing@pairtree.ai.

3) Timing & references: Expect revised invoice + credit note within 72 hours of your confirmation (we’ll aim sooner). We will include a reference: Credit Note PP-374-2025-04 and link it to your original invoice number.

4) Audit trail: We will include a short memo explaining the reason for adjustment and the test dates for your auditors.

Marcus will finalize the credit note and reissue the invoice; Jonas, please confirm with Priya that Pairtree is OK with the reconciliation approach (credit applied to taxable base).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
maria@redwood.com
[Attachment: proposed-credit-note-PP-374.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@pairtree.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Pairtree Labs Billing <billing@pairtree.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: April invoice and spike — request for retro offset & VAT handling

Hi Marissa, Jonas — thanks, this looks good and matches what our AP needs.

Pairtree confirms the test window Apr 5–11 and we agree to the credit applied to the taxable base with VAT recalculated. Please go ahead and issue the revised invoice and credit note — we need the corrected PDF for our records and to close the PO against April.

One request: can you also include a short one-line description on the credit note referencing the internal ticket number SVC-1129 so our internal auditors can match the adjustment? Otherwise, everything is approved.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Finance, Pairtree Labs
Priya.shah@pairtree.ai
